text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigeria's ruling military council introduces new civil service structure, under which a head of department, who was referred to as director-general, will now be known by the title of permanent secretary.
- Northern Kaduna state government says it has sacked civil servants who began strike action last month to back up their demand for improved conditions of service.

- Three aviation organisations have offered to intervene in the dispute between Britain and Nigeria, which has resulted in a flight ban between the two countries. The organisations are the International Civil Aviation Organisation, the European Civil Aviation Commission and the African Civil Aviation Commission.
- Opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) outlines its plans for a Thursday meeting with Commonwealth ministers in London.

- Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria lays off 363 workers in its eastern operating area. Officials say it is part of a scaling down of operations in response to a 30 percent cut in its budget by the government.
- Senior government workers warn that Nigeria should be cautious over listening to the lobby for rapid privatisation of state-owned enterprises.
- Commonwealth ministers say they have not exceeded their mandate by speaking to pro-democracy groups in discussions over Nigeria's suspension.
- Van Leer Containers attributes a downturn in the company's performance to lack of growth in the economy.
